Given: Supply frequency $f = 50\text{ Hz}$, Poles $P = 4$, Rotor frequency $f_r = 2\text{ Hz}$.

**1. Slip ($s$):**
$f_r = s \cdot f$
$$s = \frac{f_r}{f} = \frac{2}{50} = 0.04\text{ or } 4\%$$

**2. Synchronous Speed ($N_s$):**
$$N_s = \frac{120f}{P} = \frac{120 \times 50}{4} = 1500\text{ rpm}$|

**3. Motor Speed ($N$):**
$$N = N_s(1 - s) = 1500(1 - 0.04) = 1440\text{ rpm}$$
proTip: Always remember that rotor frequency is directly proportional to slip ($f_r = s f$).
